IFill.description:
A fill is an ordered list of layers, composited bottom → top
(index 0 = bottom-most, last = top-most). A semi-transparent top layer over a
media layer is how a "background tint / overlay" is expressed.

IFillLayer.description:
A single fill layer — color, gradient, image, or video.
(Historically this union WAS `IFill`; a fill is now an ordered stack of these.)

IFlowOpenValidation.description:
Verdict of {@link validateFlowForOpen}.

`safe: false` means the builder is expected to white-screen on this config,
so the caller must not open it. `problems` is human-readable and meant for
logs/diagnostics, never for end-user copy.

ILocalizable.description: A wrapper that stores per-locale values for a property.

progressBar.description:
Marks the screen as a participant in the flow's progress bar.

`enabled` is required when `progressBar` is present:
- `enabled: true` — the screen participates. In sync mode
  (`progress-bar.oneSegmentPerScreen=true`) the active segment is
  resolved by the screen's position among enabled screens (`segment`
  is omitted). In manual mode (`oneSegmentPerScreen=false`, including
  the single-segment `linear` template) `segment` references the
  bound `progress-bar-segment.customId`.
- `enabled: false` — the screen explicitly opts out.
- `progressBar` missing — equivalent to `enabled: false`.

type.description:
Sizing mode: `fixed` = explicit `value` px, `fill` = take available space,
`hug` = shrink to content.

`'auto'` is a legacy stretch idiom, not a user-selectable mode. The builder
emits it when opposing positioned anchors stretch an element, and the
transformer renders existing flows that contain it. Prefer `fill` / `hug`
in authored flows.
